articles.title: Sesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League return
articles.summary: It was a night for romance given the astonishing story that Sabah brought with them to Old Trafford for their Champions League debut. This is a club that did not even exist a decade ago and nobody saw their bolt to the title in Azerbaijan coming last season; in 2024-25, they had finished 41 points…
body: It was also a night for cold, hard reality. Manchester United were back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire.

Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City.

articles.title: Clearlake Capital close on buying out Chelsea co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter
articles.summary: Deal would value club at around £5bn. Walter is seeking to raise funds to pay off insurers. Chelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital, are closing in on an agreement to buy out co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in a deal that would see the pair make a profit on their investment and value the…
body: On-off discussions between the two ownership groups over a potential sale have been taking place for the last two years, but intensified last month as a result of Mark Walter seeking to raise funds to pay off insurers following a US federal investigation over alleged tax fraud.

Walter, Boehly and Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss all own 12.8% of Chelsea following their joint £2.5bn purchase of the club with Clearlake from Roman Abramovich four years ago, in a deal which saw the new owners commit to spending a further £1.75bn on the club.
In a statement issued to Bloomberg a spokesperson for Walter confirmed that he is seeking a sale with an agreement close.
Boehly is also expected to sell as he is a long-time investment partner of Walters. Wyss’s position is unconfirmed.

articles.title: Former University of Michigan hockey players say they were sexually hazed decades ago
articles.summary: More than a dozen ex-players are suing the University of Michigan, alleging coach and staff were aware of abuse. More than a dozen former hockey players are suing the University of Michigan, alleging their coach and other staff were aware of sexual hazing that included the forced shaving of their…
body: “The abuse was ritualized, meticulously planned and sadistic … Enduring sexual abuse was required to be a member of the Michigan men’s ice hockey team,” attorney Michael Pitt said in a sex discrimination lawsuit filed on Wednesday in federal court in Detroit.
The plaintiffs are 16 men who played at Michigan between 1984 and 2001. The lawsuit apparently grew out of conversations among several former teammates in 2024.
“To the extent any former student athlete engaged in hazing or other misconduct, they were violating university policy,” spokesperson Paul Corliss said in a written statement.

The 72-page document describes players being forced to consume excessive amounts of alcohol and eat live fish. A common allegation: they were forced to have hair around their genitals shaved by teammates. A player identified as John Doe 7 said he was taunted with a blowtorch while on a table.

articles.title: England’s Dan Lawrence delighted with form as Pakistan focus on the future
articles.summary: Lawrence rues missed ton but ‘really happy’ with displays. Tourists’ batting coach hails potential of new players. A few hours after his yelp of frustration echoed around Edgbaston, an innings of 65 and the growing conviction that “I was going to make a really big score” ended when he chased a wide…
body: “I’m obviously gutted I didn’t kick on,” he said. “I felt like I was playing really nicely and it was a really good surface to bat on against a tiring attack at that stage. I thought I was going to make a really big score, but it wasn’t meant to be. But I’m really happy with how I’ve played [this summer].

“I always knew deep down that my ability was good enough to play at this level, even though I hadn’t necessarily shown it in my first stint playing. That was obviously a tough time, when I got dropped from the team [in 2022], and all I was concentrating on was trying to score big runs in county cricket and get myself in, because I feel like I’ve got a lot to offer English cricket.”

Pakistan are also confident about their potential, even if at this stage it seems unlikely to be realised on this tour. “There’s a lot of class in this dressing room,” said Michael Smith, who was appointed batting coach last month. “There’s a lot of serious players here. It would be nice for them to show the rest of the UK, and the people back in Pakistan, what they’ve still got. Because we’ve got no doubt that it’s there.”

articles.title: McIlroy four off lead after his 'longest round'
articles.summary: Defending champion Rory McIlroy says his opening round at the Irish Open, which was played in stormy conditions and took in excess of six hours, may have been the longest of his career as he sits four behind leader Joacquin Niemann.
body: Rory McIlroy said his first round at the Irish Open at Doonbeg on Thursday may have been the longest of his career as he ended a wind-ravaged day one sitting four shots behind leader Joaquin Niemann.

McIlroy's opening one-under-par 69 took in excess of six hours as he and the rest of the field battled the high winds and sporadic showers which battered the Trump International Golf Links in County Clare.
The world number two posted birdies at the second and fourth holes, double-bogeyed the 13th after taking two shots to get out of a bunker, but then picked up a shot at the 15th.
Back-to-back Masters champion McIlroy is aiming to defend the title he won at the K Club last year and secure a third Irish Open crown of his career, having triumphed at the same venue in 2016.

articles.title: 2030 Winter Olympics boss departs amid turmoil
articles.summary: Edgar Grospiron leaves his position as president of the organising committee for the 2030 French Alps Winter Olympics just 18 months after his appointment.
body: The departure of Grospiron, the 1992 Olympic moguls champion, was confirmed at a meeting of the committee's executive board on Thursday, marking the latest setback in the event's troubled governance.

In a statement, the organising committee said: "His decision to leave the presidency is part of a deliberate, organised and fully assumed transition, taken in the interests of the project and its governance.
"It reflects a shared desire with stakeholders to enable the organisation to quickly enter this new operational phase."
Confirming his departure via a post on LinkedIn, Grospiron said his decision followed "months of tension".

articles.summary: Helping to guide Bayern Munich to a 5-0 victory over Bodø/Glimt, Vincent Kompany feels his side are starting to discover their top form and touched on Jamal Musiala's return. “We're in a good position. We still have players getting back to their rhythm.

“Everyone was happy for him [Musiala] – 75,000 people in the stadium and the people in front of their TVs. We knew his moment would come. He scored a really important goal.
"It's great for Jamal, hopefully the focus now will only be on his performances. He knows how to deal with the other topic and will continue to get all support from us," he added.

articles.title: 'A great sporting ticket' - US Open chief vows to keep day, night session format
articles.summary: US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027.
body: Tiley, who took the helm as new CEO of USTA earlier this year after leading Tennis Australia since 2013, says he has no plans for any changes to the schedule.

It comes after Ben Shelton's five-set thriller against Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals ended at 3:33am local time on Wednesday, leaving few people awake to see the near five-hour marathon reach its finale on one of the sport's biggest stages.
Players have long loved the electricity of playing night matches under the lights in the nation's biggest city.
But the tournament had already set a record with three post-2am finishes over the first six days, as well as having two other matches go past 1am.

articles.title: York Knights finish maiden Super League season with thrashing of Bradford
articles.summary: York saw off bottom club Bradford 35-16 in their final match of the regular Super League campaign at the LNER Community Stadium, where Paul Vaughan slotted over a late drop goal on his farewell appearance before retirement.
body: The Knights - looking to solidify a 10th-place finish in their debut Super League season - had Scott Galeano sent to the sin bin after just 13 minutes following a tip tackle on Phoenix Steinwede, with Bulls then having a try for full-back Caleb Aekins ruled out for a forward offload.

Ryan Sutton made the breakthrough to score the opening try for Bradford after 17 minutes, with Chris Atkin slotting over the extras. The lead, though, was short-lived as Galeano marked his return to the action by showing quick feet to then dive over.
Ben Jones-Bishop, who was given a guard of honour ahead of making his 400th career appearance, added another try for the home side, with Cody Hunter converting for a 12-6 lead.

Bradford rallied again as Riley Dean latched on to a spilled kick to touchdown, but York responded again just before half-time as Toa Mata'afa burst down the middle to send the Knights into the break 18-12 ahead.
